name: Modafinil
lead: Modafinil is a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication, often grouped as a eugeroic, that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea or shift work disorder [4]. It was developed in France by Laboratoire Lafon and is described as a related compound to adrafinil [1].

The label states that the mechanism by which modafinil promotes wakefulness is unknown, and that it has wake-promoting actions similar to sympathomimetic agents such as amphetamine and methylphenidate without an identical pharmacological profile [4]. Brain imaging work in healthy men found that it occupies the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine levels [3].

In looksmaxxing and wider self-improvement communities it is discussed as a productivity and study aid, sometimes grouped with other nootropics under "lifemaxxing" [8][9]. No published trial has tested modafinil for any facial or physical appearance outcome. Evidence on cognitive effects in healthy people is mixed in the sources reviewed, and the drug carries labelled warnings including serious rash and psychiatric symptoms [2][4].
infobox: Label: Category C; growth restriction and miscarriage reported [4]

paras: The US label lists three indications: excessive sleepiness associated with narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea and shift work disorder. For sleep apnea the label specifies that the drug treats sleepiness, not the underlying airway obstruction, and that maximal effort to use continuous positive airway pressure should come first where it is the treatment of choice [4].

Off-label interest has included depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and schizophrenia; a 2008 review described initial promise in these areas while noting the evidence base was early [2]. A network meta-analysis of ADHD medications focused on established drug classes [5].

Students, shift workers and others use modafinil without a medical indication to stay alert or study for long periods. A 2008 review of its neurochemical actions and cognitive effects discussed this literature and the question of whether any cognitive benefit exceeds simple wakefulness [2]. A registered phase 4 trial examined cognitive performance in university students [6].

The label lists serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema and anaphylaxis, multi-organ hypersensitivity, persistent sleepiness, psychiatric symptoms, effects on driving and machinery, and cardiovascular events as warnings and precautions [4]. Users on looksmax.org have described headache, appetite loss and joint aches, and one user described anxiety and sweating with the related armodafinil [8][9].

The label notes that intrauterine growth restriction and spontaneous abortion have been reported with modafinil and armodafinil, and that adequate controlled studies in pregnant women are lacking [4].

The label says the mechanism is unknown, and that modafinil-induced wakefulness can be attenuated by an alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist [4]. A 2009 imaging study in healthy men reported that modafinil binds the dopamine transporter and increases dopamine in the brain, including the nucleus accumbens [3]. A 2001 paper examined the role of dopamine in stimulant-induced wakefulness [10]. Research on the orexin system, whose loss produces a narcolepsy-like phenotype in mice, forms part of the background to wake-promoting drug research [11].
Grokipedia describes modafinil as developed in France in the 1970s by Laboratoire Lafon, emerging from work on adrafinil, with US approval following in 1998 [1].

Trials of modafinil have mostly enrolled patients with sleep disorders. The US label's indications rest on such studies [4]. A pediatric phase 3 trial studied excessive sleepiness in children and adolescents with narcolepsy [7]. Registered trials have also examined multiple sclerosis fatigue, cancer-related fatigue, post-traumatic stress disorder, remitted depression with cognitive impairment and stimulant dependence, with varying statuses including terminated and unknown [12][13][14].

A 2009 imaging study in healthy men reported effects on dopamine and the dopamine transporter [3]. A registered phase 4 trial in university students examined attention, memory and executive function in healthy participants [6]. No studies were found testing modafinil for facial or body appearance outcomes.
Modafinil is a prescription medicine in the United States [4]. Community threads discuss obtaining it without a prescription from online sellers; this wiki does not document sourcing.

Looksmax.org threads describe modafinil as an alertness aid and compare it with Adderall; users report more energy for work and study and social confidence, while others report headaches and appetite suppression [8][9]. Posters connect it to appearance indirectly, for example through leaner bulking difficulty from reduced appetite or through perceived charisma, rather than through any direct cosmetic mechanism [8][9].

timeline.event: Developed in France by Laboratoire Lafon as a derivative of adrafinil work [1].
US FDA approval for sleepiness in narcolepsy, per Grokipedia [1].
Shift work disorder indication added, per Grokipedia [1].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org modafinil appears in threads about studying, productivity and general self-improvement, often compared with Adderall [8][9].

claims.claim: Modafinil makes users more alert, productive and focused without the jitters of caffeine.
claims.believers: One poster described studying for many hours without brain fog and being less jittery than on caffeine, and another reported coworkers noticing higher productivity [8][9].
claims.experts: The label confirms wake-promoting effects in sleep-disorder patients [4]; a 2008 review found cognitive claims in healthy people less settled [2].

claims.believers: A reply in one thread flatly states it is not addictive when asked [9].
claims.experts: The mechanism involves the dopamine transporter [3], and the label includes psychiatric warnings [4]; registered trials have tested it in stimulant dependence [13].

claims.claim: Modafinil helps appearance, for example by raising charisma or social ability.
claims.believers: One poster credited it with making him more charming and awake in social settings [9].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined modafinil for appearance or social attractiveness.

claims.believers: One thread's author said prescribed Adderall had no effect for him while modafinil did [9].
claims.experts: Comparisons rest on ADHD and sleep literature, where the drugs are indicated for different conditions [4][5].

claims.claim: Modafinil carries side effects such as headaches, appetite loss and joint aches.
claims.believers: Users report throbbing headache, reduced appetite and joint pain [8].
claims.experts: The label lists serious rash, hypersensitivity, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events [4].

card.summary: Prescription wakefulness drug that forums treat as a study and productivity aid; no appearance effect has been studied.
card.note: Prescription-only in the US; label warns of serious rash and psychiatric symptoms.

quick.overview:
Modafinil is an FDA-approved prescription drug for excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing and self-improvement forums it is discussed as a way to stay alert and productive.

No trial has tested it for appearance. Posters link it to looks only indirectly, such as appetite suppression or feeling more sociable.
quick.mechanism: The label says its mechanism is unknown. A 2009 imaging study in healthy men found it binds the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine.
quick.risks: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reactions, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. Users report headache and reduced appetite. It is prescription-only in the US.
